thread.title: Can IBM’s big premium for Red Hat ignite a sustainable stock market rally? - MarketWatch

author: Nigam Arora
title: Can IBM’s big premium for Red Hat ignite a sustainable stock market rally? - MarketWatch
text:
Companies buy other companies all the time, but a 63% premium on an acquisition doesn’t happen every day.
IBM IBM, -4.34% unveiled its largest software acquisition ever by offering $190 a share for Red Hat RHT, +45.49% I need to start with a full disclosure: The Arora Report gave a signal to buy Red Hat at $43.14 with a call that it was likely to be bought out, most probably by IBM. A 63% premium on a deal is striking. Of course, a 340% gain on our position is putting me in a buying sentiment.
The anecdotal evidence is that the positive sentiment is contagious on this large premium. This is especially important since high-beta stocks like Red Hat have been hit hard. The buying is spreading. However, sellers have not gone on vacation. I have been getting lots of requests to try to figure out where is the bottom in the stock market. Let’s start with a chart.
Chart Please click here for an annotated chart of S&P 500 ETF SPY, -1.14% Somewhat similar conclusions can be drawn from the charts of the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -1.47% Nasdaq 100 ETF QQQ, -2.74% and small-cap ETF IWM, -0.77% Please note the following:
• The chart is a weekly chart to help the longer-term investor.
• The chart shows the downtrend line.
• The chart shows the support zone.
• Volume has not been high enough to have washed out weak hands. This is a negative.
• RSI (relative strength index) is very oversold.
• The chart shows RSI is more oversold than in the last correction. When the market is oversold, it often bounces.

Incomplete question Where is the bottom in the stock market? That is an incomplete question; the bottom for a day, a week, a month or forever? It is important for investors to always look at a bottom along with a time frame.
If the weak hands were washed out, the probability of this being the bottom for at least a few months would have been very high. Now, any bounce is suspect, but several positive factors are coming into play that call for a fair probability of a very short-term bottom. Investors are well-advised to remember Arora’s Second Law of Investing: “No one knows with certainty what will happen next.”
The best, and the only realistic, thing investors can do is to think in terms of probabilities.
1. The market is about to enter a seasonally strong period.
2. Midterm elections are ahead. Often elections remove uncertainty, and the market goes up irrespective of who wins.
3. Interest rates are coming down after a spike.
4. Overall the U.S. economy is staying strong.
5. If the Federal Reserve were to indicate that it will temper raising interest rates, it would spark a massive rally in stocks.
6. President Trump and President Xi of China will be meeting next month. Optimism over a trade deal may drive a rally.
Money flows Tech stocks have been the market leaders. For this reason, it makes sense to look at money flows in stocks such as Amazon AMZN, -7.76% Facebook FB, -3.36% Apple AAPL, -2.30% and Netflix NFLX, -7.16% Semiconductors are the lifeblood of the modern economy. Semiconductor stocks have been hit hard. It makes sense to pay attention to money flows in stocks such as Intel INTC, -1.62% AMD AMD, -5.56% Nvidia NVDA, -7.63% and Micron Technology MU, -3.05%
Please see “ This money-flow chart shows that Amazon and Netflix are in dangerous territory .” In interpreting money flows, many investors seem to be making several mistakes. To help them, the following points are in order:
• Money flows are dynamic. They change all the time. Nobody should make decisions today based on money flows from months ago.
• This market is under the control of the momo (momentum) crowd. For this reason, it makes sense to pay attention to the momo crowd, especially for the short term.
• The smart money (professional investors) tends to have more consistent patterns than the momo crowd.
• The momo crowd is like a yo-yo. For example, as of this writing, momo crowd money flows have become very positive in Amazon and Alibaba BABA, -6.74% and extremely positive in Tesla TSLA, +1.42% Unless you are a day trader, it is best to look at them cumulatively and smooth them with a moving average.
What to do now Setting stock market technicals aside, there is a big headwind for the stock market that many investors have not noticed. The headwind is slowing earnings growth momentum. One thing investors can do during such an environment is to focus on special situations. An example of a special situation is to consider companies that are likely to be bought out. Red Hat is in The Arora Report model portfolio and is now producing a 340% gain at a time when technology stocks are being hammered. Of course, the time to buy it was when the original buy signal was given.
The possibility of a competing bid is small, but it would not be a surprise to see the likes of Google GOOG, -5.58% GOOGL, -5.48% and Microsoft MSFT, -4.09% take a look at Red Hat for a competing bid. For this reason, there is still a buy zone for Red Hat.
Pinnacle Foods is being bought out by Conagra Brands CAG, +1.27% and is in the Arora Report model portfolio, producing a 109% gain. The plan is to hold Conagra Brands in the model portfolio. T-Mobile US TMUS, -1.38% came into the model portfolio at $12.53 when MetroPCS was bought out by T-Mobile. Now T-Mobile stock is at $66.40. Sometimes it makes sense to hold on for the long term. Our target zone on T-Mobile is $95-$110 if its merger with Sprint S, -1.71% is approved. A recent addition to the model portfolio is Esterline Technologies ESL, +0.00% which received a buyout offer from TransDigm Group TDG, -1.68% producing a 44% gain. To date, 141 stocks in The Arora Report portfolio have been bought out.
Don’t buy stocks solely for their buyout potential. Often there are a lot of rumors as part of “pump and dump” schemes and the buyouts don’t happen. Consider buying only companies that have good prospects even without buyout potential.
Buyouts are not the only special situations around. There are many special situations, such as spinoffs, new products and new markets. A good example in the marijuana industry is Canopy Growth CGC, -14.81% Many marijuana companies, such as Cronos CRON, -13.88% Tilray TLRY, -16.90% and Aurora Cannabis ACB, -17.05% have the potential to become special situations, but the stocks are very expensive. The point is that even special situations need thorough analysis. Please also see “ How one investor sidestepped this week’s stock-market decline .” Craft Brew Alliance BREW, +0.33% is another example of a special situation. If this company were to get into CBD-infused drinks in a big way, just based on sentiment, the stock could move considerably higher.
